title: Texas's 28th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Texas's 28th Congressional District pits incumbent Democratic Rep. Henry Cuellar against Republican challenger Tano Tijerina, the Webb County Judge. This South Texas district, which stretches from San Antonio to the Rio Grande Valley, has become increasingly competitive as the region has shifted to the right. Cuellar, one of the most conservative Democrats in Congress and the last Democrat to hold statewide office in Texas, was indicted in 2024 on bribery charges but received a pardon from President Trump in December 2025. Tijerina, a former Democrat who switched parties in 2024, won the Republican primary decisively with 74.3% of the vote and has been endorsed by Trump, making this a closely watched race that could help determine control of the narrowly divided House.
polling_note: No district-specific general election polls for TX-28 were found as of June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Lean Democratic.' The only available polling covers generic Texas House ballot tests, which are not specific to this district.

candidates.name: Henry Cuellar
candidates.summary: Henry Cuellar has represented Texas's 28th Congressional District since 2005 and is considered one of the most conservative Democrats in the House. A Laredo native, he previously served in the Texas House of Representatives (1987–2001) and as Texas Secretary of State (2001). Cuellar was indicted on federal bribery and money laundering charges in 2024, but President Donald Trump pardoned him in December 2025 before the case went to trial. He won the 2026 Democratic primary with 58.1% of the vote.

candidates.name: Tano Tijerina
candidates.summary: Tano E. Tijerina has served as Webb County Judge since 2015, making him the county's top elected official. A former Democrat, he switched to the Republican Party in December 2024, citing the Democratic Party's leftward shift. He won the 2026 Republican primary for Texas's 28th District with 74.3% of the vote, carrying the endorsement of President Donald Trump. Tijerina previously played Minor League Baseball after being drafted by the Milwaukee Brewers and later earned a degree from Texas A&M International University.
